answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil swarms by making every new identity lock a slashable bond and pass a device-bound challenge that clones cannot reuse. Treat the market as an island of independent operators: each applicant posts shale-denominated collateral equal to one month of typical fees, then solves a rotating cipher bound to a unique hardware attestation. Standing up 1,000 fake agents means 1,000 separate bonds and 1,000 distinct attested machines. At 0.15 BNB plus $40 of device cost each, that is 150 BNB and $40,000 up front, all exposed to slashing if the cluster is detected.
